readings.heading: Τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἑορτῆς — Mark 9:2–9
verses: 2. At that time, after six days, Jesus takes Peter and James and John, and brings them up onto a high mountain by themselves alone. And he was transfigured before them,
3. and his garments became glistening, exceedingly white as snow — such as no fuller on earth can whiten.
4. And Elijah appeared to them, together with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
5. And Peter answered and said to Jesus: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tents — one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
6. For he did not know what to say — they were terrified.
7. And a cloud came, overshadowing them; and a voice came out of the cloud: "This is my beloved Son — listen to him."
8. And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone, but Jesus alone with them.
9. And as they were coming down from the mountain, he charged them to tell no one what they had seen, until the Son of Man should rise from the dead.

readings.heading: Ὁ Ἀπόστολος — 2 Corinthians 1:12–20
verses: 12. Brothers and sisters: this is our boast — the testimony of our conscience — that we conducted ourselves in the world in the simplicity and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, and all the more toward you.
13. For we write you nothing other than what you read and also recognise — and I hope you will recognise it fully to the end,
14. just as you have recognised us in part: that we are your boast, just as you are ours, in the day of the Lord Jesus.
15. And in this confidence I intended to come to you first, so that you might have a second grace —
16. to pass through you into Macedonia, and to come back to you again from Macedonia, and to be sent on by you to Judaea.
17. So when I was planning this, was I being fickle? Or do I make my plans in a fleshly way, so that with me it is "Yes, yes" and "No, no" at the same time?
18. But as God is faithful, our word to you has not been "Yes" and "No."
19. For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you through us — through me and Silvanus and Timothy — was not "Yes" and "No"; in him it is always "Yes."
20. For all the promises of God find their "Yes" in him; and that is why through him the "Amen" is spoken, to the glory of God through us.

readings.heading: Τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον — Matthew 22:23–33
verses: 23. That same day Sadducees came to him — the ones who say there is no resurrection — and questioned him,
24. saying: "Teacher, Moses said: 'If a man dies without children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.'
25. Now there were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no offspring, left his wife to his brother.
26. Likewise the second also, and the third, up to the seventh.
27. Last of all, the woman died too.
28. So in the resurrection, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her."
29. Jesus answered them: "You are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
30. For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels of God in heaven.
31. And about the resurrection of the dead — have you not read what was spoken to you by God, saying,
32. 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living."
33. And hearing it, the crowds were astonished at his teaching.
